canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across papers, the dominant framing treats this as a failure mode in which outputs contain repeated tokens, words, phrases, sentences, or entire utterances, often described as duplicate fragments or unproductive loops that degrade meaning, readability, coherence, or conciseness. When papers specify judging criteria, they usually ask whether a response repeats itself, including repeated list items, or whether repetitive tokens or utterances affect meaning. A smaller line of work narrows the behavior to meaningless or unproductive repetition, such as continuing with repeated tokens after an answer or getting trapped in repetitive reasoning sequences on hard tasks.

Variants. Papers study it across several settings. Common variants include generic repetition in free text, duplication within summaries, and token repetition under an explicit prompt to repeat a single word; smaller lines examine dialogue "parroting" across turns, code outputs with repeated assertions or comments, translation "oscillatory hallucination," and repeated character sequences in no-space content. Some papers also describe it as emerging after excessive editing strength or under preference optimization, where outputs become overly long, repetitive, or incoherent.

Space of elicitation and scores. Only one measurement instrument is explicitly linked to it, Human evaluation, which papers use with guidelines such as checking for repetitive tokens or utterances that affect meaning. Another human-evaluation formulation asks whether the response repeats itself, including repeated list items. Some papers also describe scoring proxies rather than linked instruments, for example TTR to capture repetitiveness, TE where lower values mean many repeated tokens with poor readability, and regular-expression detection of word or character repetition.

What it is taken as evidence of. Construct-level use is sparse. Only one construct is linked, Utility preservation, and papers frame that link as related rather than as a direct indicator. Papers more often connect the behavior to other behaviors: it is related to overthinking, reward hacking, and style transfer, and one paper claims a causal relationship from repetitive generation to training data regurgitation, stating that repeated tokens can confuse models and create a vulnerability for leakage attacks.

definitions.text: An observable failure mode where the model generates repetitive tokens, phrases, or entire utterances that degrade the quality and meaning of the text.
definitions.paper: Segment-Level Diffusion: A Framework for Controllable Long-Form Generation with Diffusion Language Models

definitions.text: An observable failure mode where the model produces outputs consisting of repeating words or phrases.
definitions.paper: ReLearn: Unlearning via Learning for Large Language Models

definitions.text: Repeating similar or nearly identical actions across multiple turns in a dialogue, resulting in low response diversity despite potential goal achievement.
definitions.paper: SOTOPIA-Ω: Dynamic Strategy Injection Learning and Social Instruction Following Evaluation for Social Agents

definitions.text: Producing overly repetitive text as a failure mode after excessive editing strength.
definitions.paper: Sparse Activation Editing for Reliable Instruction Following in Narratives

definitions.text: The observable pattern of repeating phrases, sentences, or ideas without adding new information, often as a result of reward hacking in preference optimization.
definitions.paper: Weights-Rotated Preference Optimization for Large Language Models

definitions.text: The observable repetition of identical or nearly identical tokens, expressions, or comments in the generated code, such as repeated assertions or print statements.
definitions.paper: Rethinking Repetition Problems of LLMs in Code Generation

definitions.text: Producing the same input token repeatedly when prompted with a repetition task.
definitions.paper: Interpreting the Repeated Token Phenomenon in Large Language Models

definitions.text: Repeating the same or very similar information multiple times within the summary, reducing conciseness and coherence.
definitions.paper: BooookScore: A systematic exploration of book-length summarization in the era of LLMs

definitions.text: Generating repeated word sequences or repeated character sequences within no-space content.
definitions.paper: RAP: A Metric for Balancing Repetition and Performance in Open-Source Large Language Models

definitions.text: A repetitive output pattern in translation where a sequence of tokens is excessively repeated, indicating a form of degenerate generation.
definitions.paper: Mitigating Hallucinated Translations in Large Language Models with Hallucination-focused Preference Optimization

relationships.paper: Style Transfer with Multi-iteration Preference Optimization
relationships.evidence: First, we observe repetitions and hallucinations in some transferred texts. (Limitations)

naacl25: Style Transfer with Multi-iteration Preference Optimization

relationships.paper: Segment-Level Diffusion: A Framework for Controllable Long-Form Generation with Diffusion Language Models
relationships.evidence: To address this, we extend human evaluation guidelines from Clark et al. (2023), assessing repetition, fluency, coherence, compatibility (ROCStories/DialogSum), and hallucination (DeliData): (Section 4.2)

acl25: Segment-Level Diffusion: A Framework for Controllable Long-Form Generation with Diffusion Language Models

relationships.evidence: We observed that with enough training compute, the model started to show signs of reward hacking, where it increased the lengths of its CoTs on hard questions using repetition rather than learning to solve them. (Section 4.6)

relationships.paper: Interpreting the Repeated Token Phenomenon in Large Language Models
relationships.evidence: Nasr et al. (2023) first observed that repeated tokens could confuse models, creating a vulnerability exploitable for training data leakage attacks. (Section 5)

icml25: Interpreting the Repeated Token Phenomenon in Large Language Models
